title: Change-impact skill
summary: Trace the parts of a system affected by a proposed change and identify what needs verification.

sections.label: Inputs
sections.text: The proposed outcome, known component and data dependencies, relevant versions, consumer contracts and existing checks.

sections.label: Graph application example
sections.text: For an RDF application, the inputs may include ontology concepts, TTL and query locations, service revisions and API consumers. These are one implementation of the general dependency investigation.

sections.label: Procedure
sections.text: Follow known relationships and actual references. Identify direct effects, migrations, consumer contracts, and test scenarios. Label indirect impacts as hypotheses until checked.

sections.label: Output
sections.text: Affected component map, dependency order, suggested verification, and evidence for each impact.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: A claimed impact links to a source relationship, code reference, contract, or executed observation.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
sections.text: Use the existing Architecture and impact connection to trace the proposed change against the baseline and affected consumer contracts. The workflow placement and checks are Atlas recommendations. Only the source contribution below was verified on 15 October 2026, not every original assertion or project outcome.

sections.label: Gap review: acceptance outputs
items: An impact map links each claimed affected component or contract to an inspected reference and its revision.
The assessment lists migration and consumer verification needs, separating direct evidence from indirect hypotheses.
A reviewer checks the baseline and approves, rejects or leaves unresolved each material impact before implementation.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: NASA describes assessing requirements changes against a documented baseline before approval and implementation. The source supports the change assessment practice. It does not establish the actual dependencies, required approvals or effects of this project. Review date: 15 October 2026. This review covers this source contribution only, not the whole guide.

catalog.applicability: Use when a proposed change needs its affected components, migrations, consumer contracts and test scenarios traced and the needed verification identified. Label indirect impacts as hypotheses until a source relationship, code reference, contract or executed observation supports them.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
